content: 1. In individuals with drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis (TB), the use of 4-month fluoroquinolone-containing regimens is not recommended. Instead, the 6-month rifampicin-based regimen (2HRZE/4HR) remains the standard treatment. This recommendation is strong, with moderate certainty in the evidence. 2. The use of fixed-dose combination tablets is preferred over separate drug formulations for the treatment of drug-susceptible TB. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty in the evidence. 3. For all individuals with drug-susceptible pulmonary TB, thrice-weekly dosing is not recommended during either the intensive or continuation phases of therapy. Daily dosing remains the recommended frequency. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 4. In individuals with drug-susceptible pulmonary TB who are living with HIV and receiving antiretroviral therapy during TB treatment, a 6-month standard treatment regimen is recommended over an extended treatment duration of 8 months or more. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 5. For individuals with tuberculous meningitis, initial adjuvant corticosteroid therapy with dexamethasone or prednisolone tapered over 6–8 weeks is recommended. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty in the evidence. 6. In individuals with tuberculous pericarditis, initial adjuvant corticosteroid therapy may be used. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 7. For individuals requiring TB retreatment, the Category II regimen should no longer be prescribed. Instead, drug-susceptibility testing should be conducted to guide the choice of treatment regimen. This is a good practice statement. 8. The treatment of drug-resistant TB should follow similar principles to the treatment of drug-susceptible TB. Individuals with drug-resistant TB have the same right to health, and ethical obligations should overcome any barriers to diagnosis and treatment. Ensuring treatment adherence through tailored interventions is critical. 9. Specialized care is required for individuals with drug-resistant TB, which is often not feasible during the initial phase of an emergency. These patients should be referred to appropriate services outside the emergency setting. 10. Surgery may be required as an adjunct to medical treatment for individuals with drug-resistant TB. This includes elective partial lung resection (lobectomy or wedge resection) to reduce bacterial load and improve prognosis. Patients should be referred to experienced surgical services. 11. Palliative care for individuals with drug-resistant TB is essential to address suffering caused by the disease, treatment toxicity, and sequelae. Those with extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB) should be prioritized for palliative care, as they often remain infectious and require proper infection control measures. 12. The detection and management of drug-resistant and XDR-TB depend on the capacity of health services, which is typically developed during the stabilization phase of an emergency. 13. A shorter all-oral bedaquiline-containing regimen of 9–12 months is recommended for eligible individuals with confirmed multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant TB (MDR/RR-TB) who have not been exposed to second-line TB medicines in this regimen for more than 1 month and in whom fluoroquinolone resistance has been excluded. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 14. For individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens, all three Group A agents and at least one Group B agent should be included to ensure treatment starts with at least four effective TB agents. If only one or two Group A agents are used, both Group B agents should be included. Group C agents may be added if necessary. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 15. Kanamycin and capreomycin should not be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 16. Levofloxacin or moxifloxacin should be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty in the evidence. 17. Bedaquiline should be included in longer MDR-TB regimens for individuals aged 18 years or older. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty in the evidence. 18. Bedaquiline may also be included in longer MDR-TB regimens for individuals aged 6–17 years. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 19. Linezolid should be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty in the evidence. 20. Clofazimine and cycloserine or terizidone may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 21. Ethambutol may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 22. Delamanid may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB aged 3 years or older on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with moderate certainty in the evidence. 23. Pyrazinamide may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 24. Imipenem-cilastatin or meropenem may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 25. Amikacin may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB aged 18 years or older on longer regimens when susceptibility has been demonstrated and adverse reactions can be adequately monitored. If amikacin is unavailable, streptomycin may replace it under the same conditions. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 26. Ethionamide or prothionamide may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens only if bedaquiline, linezolid, clofazimine, or delamanid are not used, or if better options are not available. This is a conditional recommendation against use, with very low certainty in the evidence. 27. Para-aminosalicylic acid may be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens only if bedaquiline, linezolid, clofazimine, or delamanid are not used, or if better options are not available. This is a conditional recommendation against use, with very low certainty in the evidence. 28. Clavulanic acid should not be included in the treatment of individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens. This is a strong recommendation against use, with low certainty in the evidence. 29. For individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens, a total treatment duration of 18–20 months is suggested for most patients, with modifications based on the patient’s response to therapy. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 30. For individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens, a treatment duration of 15–17 months after culture conversion is suggested for most patients, with modifications based on the patient’s response to therapy. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 31. For individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens containing amikacin or streptomycin, an intensive phase of 6–7 months is suggested for most patients, with modifications based on the patient’s response to therapy. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 32. A treatment regimen lasting 6–9 months, composed of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL), may be used under operational research conditions in individuals with MDR-TB resistant to fluoroquinolones, who have had no prior exposure to bedaquiline and linezolid or have been exposed for no more than 2 weeks. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 33. In individuals with MDR/RR-TB on longer regimens, sputum culture in addition to sputum smear microscopy is recommended to monitor treatment response. Monthly sputum culture is desirable. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty in the evidence. 34. Elective partial lung resection (lobectomy or wedge resection) may be used alongside a recommended MDR-TB regimen in individuals with MDR-TB. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty in the evidence. 35. Health education and counseling on the disease and treatment adherence should be provided to individuals on TB treatment. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty in the evidence. 36. A package of treatment adherence interventions may be offered to individuals on TB treatment, alongside the selection of a suitable treatment administration option. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty in the evidence.
